newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Air top cargo capacity provider.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Air top cargo capacity provider.

text.p: Northwest Airlines flew more cargo capacity across the Pacific than any other airline last year, statistics published by the MergeGlobal air cargo consultancy show.

Northwest, which operates seven Boeing 747-200 freighters on the Pacific in addition to bellyhold capacity on passenger flights, was capacity leader eastbound and westbound between the U.S. and North Asia.
Northwest also was capacity leader from Southeast Asia to the U.S. and second to Korean Airlines, from the U.S. to Southeast Asia, said MergeGlobal.
Last year, Northwest boosted capacity by 13.1 percent from the U.S. to North Asia, by 9.7 percent from North Asia to the U.S., by 116.2 percent from Southeast Asia to the U.S. and 307.6 percent.
Northwest's total Pacific capacity rose 38 percent to 330.4 million kgs, moving the U.S. carrier ahead of Japan Airlines Ltd, at 291 million kgs. Federal Express Corp was third at 257.3 million kgs.
In 1995, JAL was Pacific capacity leader with 309.9 million kgs, followed by Northwest with 239 million kgs.
Back in 1993, Japan Airlines was capacity leader on the Pacific, but four years of a strong yen and consequent restructuring of its freighter fleet contributed to JAL's fall to second.
That triple digit growth by Northwest to Southeast Asia reflected increased passenger flights to Southeast Asia and increased freighter flying overall.

According to MergeGlobal, Korean Air cut capacity from the U.S. to Southeast Asia by 14.6 percent - 58.1 million kgs versus 68 million kgs in 1995 - but boosted capacity from Southeast Asia to the U.S. by 42.9 percent, from the U.S. to North Asia by 148 percent and from North Asia to the U.S. by 49.8 percent.

Forced to cope with the yen's strength, JAL increased capacity between the U.S. and North Asia by 9.6 percent to 193 million kgs to take advantage of stronger yields on those corridors while reducing capacity between the U.S. and Southeast Asia by almost 27 percent to 97 million kgs.

Smaller carriers continued to make their presence felt. Taiwan's EVA Air joined the top ten carriers between North Asia and the US. EVA offered almost 53.8 million kgs from North Asia to the US, up 50.9 percent. In four years, EVA has increased its North Asia-US capacity fivefold, the study showed. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
